cases.question: ¿Qué diferencias hay entre la cal aérea y la cal hidráulica natural para trabajar sobre muros antiguos?

httpResponse.answer: La cal aérea es muy transpirable y tradicional, pero fragua lentamente y es menos apropiada para capas gruesas sobre soportes húmedos o débiles. La cal hidráulica natural (NHL 2 o NHL 3.5) se considera más compatible con piedra, tierra y fábricas antiguas; fragua también con la humedad ambiental y mantiene una rigidez moderada [S1].

cases.question: I want to renovate changing rooms in a sports centre that remains open. What should I check to carry out the work in phases?

httpResponse.answer: Check that each phase is compatible with hygiene, access, escape routes and continued use; pay particular attention to water, wet-surface slipping risks and services [S3]. Also check ventilation, moisture, gradients, drainage, slip-resistant finishes, accessibility and maintenance, and verify the specific public-use and safety requirements [S1]. Sequence work from safety, leaks and services through healthy conditions, waterproofing and substrates to finishes, and confirm that phasing will not require repeated demolition or compromise technical solutions [S4].
